notes: Dahli taluka was carved out of Chachro taluka between 1998 and 2017, but no source giving the year of its creation was found. Second pass: Not dated. Narrowed: Dawn 14 Jun 2016 (dawn.com/news/1264627) reports Kaloi notified on 13 Jun 2016 as the SEVENTH taluka of Tharparkar, so Dahli (the sixth) existed by June 2016; the NDMA 'Drought Situation Report of Sindh Particularly in District Tharparkar-2018' (12 Nov 2018; cited in the Wikipedia Tharparkar article's rainfall table, link now dead and not in the Wayback Machine) marks Dahli 'taluka not created' for 2014 and gives it rainfall data from 2015. Dahli therefore appears to have been created in 2015 (or late 2014), but no primary source or news report of the notification was found (Dawn, Tribune, Jang, Wikipedia English/Sindhi, Sindh Atlas, ECP all checked).

Islamkot taluka was carved out of Mithi taluka between 1998 and 2017, but no source giving the year of its creation was found. Second pass: Not dated. Narrowed: Tharparkar still had four talukas (Mithi, Diplo, Nagarparkar, Chhachhro) at the Oct 2005 taluka nazim oath-taking (Dawn 18 Oct 2005, dawn.com/news/161666) and in Nov 2008 only the mukhtiarkars of those four talukas reported on drought (Dawn 2 Nov 2008, dawn.com/news/amp/328117); Islamkot is treated as a taluka with its own rainfall record from 2014 in the NDMA Tharparkar drought report of 2018 (via Wikipedia, link dead) and was the fifth taluka before Dahli (sixth) and Kaloi (seventh, 13 Jun 2016). Creation therefore falls between Nov 2008 and 2014; no notification date found in Dawn, Tribune, Business Recorder, Jang, Wikipedia English/Sindhi or Sindh Atlas.

No boundary event: the 1998 tables abbreviate the name as K.N. Shah and the 2017 tables spell it Khairpur Nathan Shah. PBS's 2017 Sindh tehsil table lists KHAIRPUR NATHAN SHAH TALUKA (Dadu) with a 1998 comparison population of 253,309 for the same unit, confirming continuity. (second research pass)
